Sometimes you come across albums that make you feel, from the very first listen, that “this is something special”. Wearing Words , Emily Wittbrodt ‘s new album, released in 2026 on impressive Belgian label Futura Resistenza, is one such rarity. The Cologne-based cellist, composer and singer effortlessly blurs the boundaries between classical, pop, improv and chamber music, and builds an own universe in which each melody and every word falls precisely in its place. Language is central to Wearing Words : songs that grow out of sound, rhythm and meaning, as fragile as they are powerful. Sandro Hähnel ‘s soft, almost genderless voice gives Wittbrodt’s compositions a touching eloquence. Think: the lush emotion of Rufus Wainwright , the vulnerability of Anohni , and a subtle baroque grandeur that sounds completely contemporary. Cello, piano, synthesizers, accordion, clarinet and refined arrangements flow together to form a rich, dreamy listening experience in which a sense of wonder is never far removed. Music that reveals itself slowly, but lingers long in the mind. For those who love discovering new musical worlds: let yourself be carried away by one of the most intriguing albums of the moment and experience Wearing Words live. A concert to take your breath away.
0881A82B367883B4CA5BA63F6538C727: Warhaus unveils “Simple Pleasures” today, a lead single confirming the release of ‘The Donkey’, his fifth studio album. With this, he also announces a new European tour which will, of course, include a stop here. It takes just a few notes to recognise Warhaus. Since 2016’s ‘We F****d a Flame Into Being’, Maarten Devoldere’s solo project has forged a distinctive identity, somewhere between sophisticated pop, melancholy and darkness. He continued along these lines with ‘Warhaus’ (2017), ‘Ha Ha Heartbreak’ (2022) and ‘Karaoke Moon’ in 2024. With ‘The Donkey’, however, the artist seems ready to push boundaries and explore a more instinctive direction. In collaboration with his long-standing partner and producer Jasper Maekelberg, Warhaus delves deeper into electronica, featuring dark synths, trip-hop influences and tribal rhythms inspired by South African Gqom. Following the atmospheric and unsettling teaser ‘The Baby’, which he treated us to last August, he now presents ‘Simple Pleasures’: a debut single that transports you into a feverish nocturnal dream. With this, Warhaus reveals a new, elegant, sensual and danceable side to his artistic journey, yet always retaining that characteristic, slightly strange undertone that defines his universe. In his live performances, Maarten Devoldere aims to embrace both facets, weaving the new tracks from ‘The Donkey’ into the classics from his repertoire.
08B0704DD67BF70BFCE66AF0E35EA12E: After a final run of shows in France, including a sold-out Olympia and two sold-out Salle Pleyel performances, aupinard returns to stages with a brand-new live show, still driven by the intensity and warmth that make his concerts so unique. On this occasion, he will present spleen. social club , his very first album: a project that reflects who he is free, radiant, and impossible to categorize. Blending bossa nova , soul , and electronic music , the Bordeaux-born artist explores all of his influences with rare sincerity. Conceived as a vibrant and collaborative project alongside Anaïs Cardot , Ino Casablanca , and Sonny Rave , spleen. social club stands out as the soundtrack of a generation without musical boundaries.

Music critics and peers were already taking note of her name in a big way even before she released her first album. The public got to know Camille Yembe through her debut EP Plastique, her performance at Couleur Café, or perhaps thanks to the prestigious Music Moves Europe Award that the 29-year-old pop singer won earlier this year.

Among her fans from the very beginning are the cream of Brussels’ music exports: Angèle, Stromae and Damso. And rightly so, because the Brussels-based artist with Congolese roots makes music that touches the soul: an intense blend of soul, alternative pop and R&B, underpinned by honest lyrics and a voice that sounds both powerful and fragile.

In her music, Camille explores themes such as identity, womanhood, love, insecurity and self-acceptance. She does so without filters: personally, emotionally and straight from the heart. On her debut album Jeune & Laide, she reveals herself to be both vulnerable and combative, with songs that oscillate between minimalist melancholy and grand emotional outbursts.

Live, Camille Yembe effortlessly translates that intimacy to the stage. Don’t expect a conventional pop show, but a compelling performance in which emotion, presence and musicality take centre stage. With appearances at festivals such as Dour Festival and Les Nuits Botanique, and growing attention from the Belgian and French music scenes, she is rapidly emerging as an artist you simply must see live.

Lela Soto is one of the most established and promising young voices on the contemporary flamenco scene. Although born in Madrid, her singing is deeply rooted in the tradition of Jerez de la Frontera. Lela combines her family heritage – from her grandfather Sordera to her uncle Ray Heredia – with her own musical interests to create a highly personal, fresh interpretation of ‘cante’.

Last year she released her debut album El Fuego Que Llevo Dentro, accompanied by over 50 concerts across Europe (including Primavera, Roadburn, etc.) and glowing reviews from the specialist press (TVE News, El País, Billboard. El Cultural (El Mundo). A new album is due out in spring 2027, and we’ll have the chance to discover it during her very first concert in our country.

anaiis is a London-based French-Senegalese artist whose sound blends neo-soul, R&B and jazz. Born in Toulouse, she grew up between Dakar, Dublin and Oakland. The work of artists and thinkers such as Ella Fitzgerald, Nina Simone , James Baldwin , bell hooks and Octavia Butler helped her find her own voice.

Her debut EP, Nina , was released in 2018. Since then, she has performed alongside artists including Erykah Badu and toured as a support act for Daniel Caesar and Mereba .

Her album Devotion & The Black Divine centres on the journey of coming home to oneself. The album explores identity, motherhood, knowledge and self-acceptance. On tracks such as Sunshine and P4P , joy and anger, pleasure and justice come together. Live, this translates into an intimate, warm performance driven by powerful vocals and live instrumentation.

“Her powerful voice soothes with words of affirmation over a soft, skipping neo-soul bassline.” ( Crack Magazine)

At the age of thirty, Pomme is embarking on a new chapter with La Forteresse, her fifth album, for which she has, for the first time, taken sole artistic charge. Surrounded by her fellow musicians, she has created an intimate yet ambitious work.

The album unfolds in four chapters: childhood, love and trauma, crossing the wall, and finally arriving on the other side, all driven by a fictional creature that is half-human, half-bat. Once taken in by humans, she has lived locked away for centuries in a fortress until she decides to scale its walls.

Pomme has immersed herself in medieval folklore, the paintings of Hieronymus Bosch, the musicals of Jacques Demy and Michel Legrand, the performances of La Horde and Peeping Tom, as well as the films of Miyazaki. Blending stripped-back folk, richer arrangements and influences ranging from the medieval to the cinematic and dreamlike, Pomme tackles personal and societal issues head-on: her difficult start in the music industry, the loneliness of the outsider, exhaustion linked to hyperactivity, the symbolic milestone of turning thirty, ecological anxiety, and contemporary models of romance.

Opening act: Bells Larsen Somewhere between lo-fi indie and folk ballads, Bells Larsen’s meticulously crafted arrangements bring to mind Elliott Smith, Sufjan Stevens and Adrienne Lenker, whilst her lyrics reflect on sibling dynamics, the creation of a queer world and shared epiphanies, all wrapped in soundscapes of quiet intimacy.

This session will take place at GC Ten Weyngaert , Bondgenotenstraat 54, 1190 Vorst. Doors open at 7.30 pm and we’ll start singing at 8.00 pm. The session is scheduled to finish at 9.30 pm.

Do you want to improve your Dutch and do you enjoy singing? Then you’ve come to the right place! Every month, accompanied by two musicians and a set list full of Dutch-language classics, we head to a different community centre in Brussels. There, we practise Dutch together – through singing!

Through Dutch-language songs, you’ll get to know the language better in a fun and accessible way. At the same time, you’ll discover more about Belgian culture and meet new people. Three birds with one stone!

And don’t worry: you don’t need to be Ann Christy or Clouseau. Fun and enthusiasm are what matter most. You don’t need to be a talented singer!

We’ll provide a pianist, a lead singer, the song lyrics and a free drink. Everyone’s welcome and the sessions are free. Registration is required, though.

Take a look at our schedule and find out when we’ll be singing near you. Fancy warming up your vocal cords in the meantime? Check out this season’s setlist here !

In collaboration with the Taalunie , Theater van A tot Z and the Flemish Community Commission (VGC).

In barely a year, the Polish band Omasta played more than a hundred concerts across Europe. Those hours spent on the road, on stage, backstage and together are reflected on Hits Different, the second album by this Kraków-based collective.

On Hits Different, Omasta builds on the sound of their debut, Jazz Report From The Hood, whilst at the same time breaking new ground. Jazz blends with hip-hop, beats from Detroit and Los Angeles, and the warm sounds of 1970s fusion. Yet the album sounds different from its predecessor. There’s more scope for electronic elements, the tracks sometimes take unexpected turns, and improvisation still plays a major role. Whilst the debut drew on the band members’ personal stories and emotions, Hits Different adopts the narrator’s perspective. The album feels like a film, with tracks that shift between happiness, excitement, tension and disorientation. The music never tells the whole story, but leaves room for your own interpretation. One thing is clear, though: this story doesn’t end with a happy ending.

Live, you can expect a catchy mix of jazz, hip-hop, grooves and improvisation. No two shows are the same, so you don’t want to miss this!

From whispered secrets to millions of streams: the French phenomenon Isïa spread like wildfire. With her radiant voice and a talent for catchy phrasing, she quickly established her own sound on the new French pop scene, transforming intimate moments into bittersweet anthems.

Her meteoric rise reached a peak with the release of her debut EP, Plein d’agrafes, at the end of February. A modern, meticulously crafted record that embraces her vulnerabilities and reveals a unique artist. On stage, the audience responded with immediate enthusiasm: she instantly filled La Boule Noire and Les Étoiles, two prestigious Parisian venues where she performed this sensitive and delicate debut project. Isïa has taken her time to develop her talent, but her moment has now arrived. Don’t miss her first concert in Belgium!

Enter the world of Adam La Nuit , where rumba, chanson, poetry and alternative pop come together. This Belgian-Congolese artist makes music about growing up between worlds, languages, families and different versions of yourself.

His universe runs through Kinshasa, Liège and Brussels . Kinshasa is the childhood paradise that still lives on in his music as a vivid memory. Liège represents adolescence, returning to Europe, solitude, rebellion, parties, music and the start of finding his own voice as an artist.

Family, memory, identity, desire and everything we inherit from the people before us all find their way into his music. His songs move between celebration and solitude, softness and intensity, romance and survival, the personal and the political.

He describes his work as a form of magical realism : a space where day and night meet, where the sun rises while the moon and stars are still visible. His stage name reflects this idea: in the night, the stars become visible.

His world is sensual, spiritual and cinematic, with influences ranging from Alexander McQueen and Frank Ocean to Mbilia Bel .

Adam La Nuit brings his latest album Entre Nous/Deux to AB Club. You’re gonna want to be there!
5DD3E3DAF0F8978E6B4C46E27BDFD68C: It wasn't a premidated choice, but we couldn't have dreamed of a better evening for the soothing tunes of Indonesian trio Thee Marloes . Anyone who loves smooth, heartwarming classic soul shouldn't miss this night—whether accompanied by a loved one or not. Thee Marloes have made a breakthrough in the Indonesian music scene. This musical gem from Surabaya blends soul, jazz, and pop with a subtle Indonesian twist. Natassya Sianturi (vocals/keys), Sinatrya Dharaka (guitar), and Tommy Satwick (drums) released their debut album, Perak , via Big Crown Records, gathering international attention with their infectious grooves and warm ballads. Lyrically, it reflects the past two years of their lives: social realities, evolving love lives, and personal issues that clash with public identities. Rather than explicitly explaining these tensions, the songs aim to make them palpable. Come and experience for yourself just how well they succeed. Love will be in the air for sure!

Following the success of his new album Roads vol. 3 and after selling out the AB (Brussels) and the OM (Liège) in January, Thylacine has already announced his return to Brussels! To mark the occasion, he’ll be returning to rock the capital with two new dates.

Sometimes you have to uproot yourself to find harmony with yourself and the world around you. It is certainly based on this principle that Thylacine has decided to continue his creative quest. For his new album, ‘Roads vol. 3,’ the artist decided to step away once again from the creative routines of his Paris studio. He, who admits to struggling to compose two tracks in a single location, decided this time to spend three months exploring a new continent. William Rezé-Thylacine gave himself the time he needed—the time that’s missing when you’re bogged down in the routine and rhythm of touring, the time required for travel to become an authentic experience and for intuition to transform into something ever more daring and original. This album is the embodiment of an astonishing journey. A veritable creative whirlwind, the result of profound reflections on his art and practice in the face of the delicate balances of the world around him. A new musical odyssey that makes Thylacine a fundamentally one-of-a-kind artist.

Support : Cécile Lacharme Cécile Lacharme explores the cello with a sensitive and modern approach as the unique musician that she is.

With Black Koyo , saxophonist Mattias De Craene brings together the Moroccan Gnawa tradition and his own musical world. The project emerged from his travels between Morocco and Brussels and weaves traditional rhythms and chants with saxophone, loops, and electronics. The result: a captivating musical journey centered on rhythm, breath, and sound.

Led by Maalem Hicham Bilali , the Brussels-based ensemble Black Koyo brings together the distinctive sounds of the guibri, qraqueb, and call-and-response chants with De Craene’s saxophone and electronics. Norwegian producer and musician Jan Bang , who mixed the album, adds his signature approach to live sampling, blending electronics, improvisation, rhythm, and texture.

The music moves between tradition and experimentation, ranging from subdued passages to compelling, rhythmic outbursts. Gnawa, saxophone, and electronics converge in a sound that is both traditional and innovative. “A compelling work. Live, it’s even more powerful.” (De Standaard)

Members Mattias De Craene - saxophone, electronics Hicham Bilali - guibri, vocals, qraqueb Ismael Akhraz - vocals, qraqueb Marwan Abantor - vocals, qraqueb
82ACF679CCDF77FA30D736ED5C1D65C7: What happens when two restless seekers of sound find one another at the meeting place of tradition and experiment? Iztok Koren and Raphael Rogiński transform that encounter into a living landscape in which folklore, improvisation and imagination blur. Their music is rooted in a deep respect for old sounds, but refuses to be pinned down by any single tradition. The result: a constantly transforming polyphony, rich in texture, nuance and tension. With an arsenal of unconventional playing techniques and a fascination for alternative vocal systems, they construct a universe that feels archaic and futuristic at the same time. Their musical interplay is organic and intuitive, like a conversation without words. They themselves describe it as a “Byzantine-steppe tale” , a contemporary narration rooted in folklore, yet resolutely looking ahead. Live, that world unfolds as a hypnotic trip through unknown realms, a sonic tapestry in which cultures, ideas and voices converge in a language that transcends boundaries. Together, Koren and Rogiński find a shared sound that chafes, connects and continues to resonate, long after that last note has died away. Iztok Koren Slovenian multi-instrumentalist Iztok Koren has been venturing off the beaten track for years now. From the playful post-rock of ŠKM banda to the raw noisecore duo Hexenbrutal and the internationally acclaimed freak-folk trio Širom : he’s always pushing the boundaries.
851B36C2F8703A77881A51BD2ED12735: With ‘Figures’, Noa Lee returns following their critically acclaimed debut ‘Airship’. The Brussels-based band, fronted by singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Nina Kortekaas (see also Sylvie Kreusch, Portland, Eefje De Visser), has built up a strong reputation within the Belgian indie pop scene over recent years. The music conjures up images of night-time dancefloors, deserted motorways and moments where melancholy and euphoria meet. Live, Noa Lee brings that world to life with a compelling set that balances tranquillity and release. A concert for anyone who loves to be swept away by adventurous and cinematic indie pop.

Cameron Whitcomb grew up in British Columbia, on Canada’s west coast. At the age of seventeen, he left home to work on a pipeline, where he discovered his passion for singing. That moment laid the foundations for his debut EP ‘Quitter’, in which he speaks candidly about overcoming his addiction. Since then, his music has reached a global audience, racking up over 835 million streams and 7.4 million monthly listeners on Spotify.

His debut album ‘The Hard Way’ even reached number one in the Country Albums chart. In early 2025, he also made his definitive breakthrough in Belgium with his single “Medusa”. On his latest EP, ‘Deep Water’, he delves further into songwriting, featuring, amongst other tracks, the viral hit “Kingdom of Fear”.

JPEGMAFIA , or Peggy as he is commonly known, was born in New York to Jamaican parents, but moved constantly from one place to another due to difficult circumstances at home. After finishing secondary school, JPEGMAFIA joined the US Army. He was deployed to various parts of the world and eventually took part in the Iraq War. These experiences added new dimensions to his repertoire as a producer and rapper. He does everything himself: from writing and recording to producing, mixing and mastering all his music. JPEGMAFIA’s sound is dark, yet never without a touch of humour that only serves to heighten the unease. His role as villain or satirist, protector of the streets or nihilist is deliberately difficult to pin down.

Peggy makes a point of insulting his fans as much as possible, but at the same time he always makes it clear that he loves his fans. What’s more, he proves time and time again that he’s even better live than on record!

Compro Oro has been touring the world for over ten years. The Ghent-based collective draws on jazz and psychedelia for its unique soundscape, enriched with influences from global sounds from every corner of the globe. From Havana to Mogadishu to Istanbul: every album brings fresh musical inspiration, featuring groovy songs, colourful melodies, and the marimba and vibraphone taking centre stage. On Buy The Dip (2022), the band added a generous dash of synths and electronic effects, with the crypto world as their target.

For their latest project, the Ghent-based band are heading to Kinshasa. To this end, they’ve joined forces with the Congolese likembé player, vocalist and dancer Bouton Kalanda , who also regularly collaborates with Alain Platel and Fabrizio Cassol. With his warm (bass) likembé and intriguing vocals in Lingala , he gives the quintet’s layered sound a fresh twist. Think: Konono N1 meets a stylish jazz twist, with that recognisable Compro Oro groove running through it all.

This new musical direction is being unveiled in two phases: the EP Lamellomania was released in January 2026, followed by the full album on 29 January 2027. Both releases are out via W.E.R.F. Records . Expect new grooves, unexpected musical detours and, above all, plenty of energy to get you moving.

Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul open a new chapter. Following the internationally acclaimed Topical Dancer , the Belgian duo returns with Mainland Madinina , an album that took shape between Belgium and Martinique and was again co-produced by Soulwax.

Their quirky mix of electro-pop, house, synth-pop and post-punk saw Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul become one of Belgium’s most striking acts over recent years. Their sharp humour and socially critical perspective earned them praise from the likes of Pitchfork, The Guardian and BBC 6 Music. They also conquered international stages, from Glastonbury and Sónar to Pitchfork Festival Chicago and Later... with Jools Holland.

On Mainland Madinina , they broaden their horizons once again. Themes like grief, parenthood, migration and colonial legacies form the common thread through an album that sounds both personal and adventurous. Adigéry gives us her strongest vocal performance to date. Her emotional openness goes hand in hand with the playful, provocative energy that makes the duo so appealing.

Those who have seen Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul perform live know that their concerts are much more than just a gig. They are an exuberant celebration in which urgency, humour, danceability and unexpected twists converge. In February 2027, they will embark on an international tour to present Mainland Madinina live.
9A5102EEEE49909E30059B8DCAFCC9FB: Isaac Roux (BE) writes songs about the moment when youth slowly gives way to something that looks like maturity. Nostalgia for adolescence creeps into his music, as does the realisation that growing up is never easy. After visits to Pukkelpop, Rock Werchter, Eurosonic and the release of his debut album Troubled Waters (2024), Isaac Roux is intentionally seeking out the fringes. His sound is becoming looser, faster and more lo-fi: wailing guitars, rebellious arrangements and rhythms that keep driving forward. There are echoes of Beach Fossils , the melancholy of The Cure and the dreamy, psychedelic layers of Tame Impala . Always filtered through his own, unpolished vision. On Young Hearts , Isaac Roux gives a first glimpse into a new chapter. The track is a powerful anthem of rebellion and authenticity, that calls for conventions to be broken and fully embracing one’s own voice. To create the recordings, the band retreated to a small house at the foot of the Mont Ventoux, where they set up an entire DIY recording process under the banner ‘Studio La Pichounette’. This approach resulted in a rawer, more direct sound with a distinct sense of band chemistry. These recording sessions then received their final mix in collaboration with Peter Katis ( The National , Interpol , Kurt Vile , Death Cab for Cutie ). Together with producer Bert Vliegen , Louis De Roo headed to Bridgeport to put the finishing touches on the tracks, at a studio rich in history.

They draw inspiration from the dark history of heavy music, but put their own distinctive spin on it. “The Scientist isn’t just mixing - he’s conducting a sonic symphony.” (Rolling Stone)

“A visionary who turned dials into instruments and studios into galaxies.” (The Guardian)

Hopeton Brown – known worldwide as The Scientist Dubmaster – is hailed as one of the most innovative and influential pioneers in the field of reggae, and more specifically dub. The Scientist began his career in the late 1970s in Kingston (Jamaica) at the iconic studios of that other dub legend: King Tubby . There, he brought a new dimension to the art of mixing: he turned the mixing desk into a living instrument with which sound itself could be reshaped, recomposed and reimagined. With his unmistakable hallmarks – deep basslines, spacious echoes and a hypnotic reverb – The Scientist redefined the dub landscape.

The Scientist collaborated with some of reggae’s most iconic voices, including Barrington Levy, Roots Radics, Johnny Osbourne and Augustus Pablo , whilst continually inspiring new generations in reggae, hip-hop and electronic music. In 2010, The Scientist even ventured into a remix of Lady Gaga’s (featuring Beyoncé ) ‘Telephone’.

His groundbreaking albums – Scientist Wins the World Cup (1982), Heavyweight Dub Champion (1980) and Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires (1981) – remain timeless milestones in the genre. It is this last album that The Scientist will perform in its entirety ‘in the round’ – that is to say, in the centre of the venue, surrounded by the audience.

For reasons beyond our control, the two Thylacine concerts at AB will be merged into one single concert on Friday, February 26, 2027. As a result, the concert scheduled for Saturday, February 27 will no longer take place. ---

Following the success of his new album Roads vol. 3 and after selling out the AB (Brussels) and the OM (Liège) in January, Thylacine has already announced his return to Brussels! To mark the occasion, he’ll be returning to rock the capital with two new dates.

Sometimes you have to uproot yourself to find harmony with yourself and the world around you. It is certainly based on this principle that Thylacine has decided to continue his creative quest. For his new album, ‘Roads vol. 3,’ the artist decided to step away once again from the creative routines of his Paris studio. He, who admits to struggling to compose two tracks in a single location, decided this time to spend three months exploring a new continent. William Rezé-Thylacine gave himself the time he needed—the time that’s missing when you’re bogged down in the routine and rhythm of touring, the time required for travel to become an authentic experience and for intuition to transform into something ever more daring and original. This album is the embodiment of an astonishing journey. A veritable creative whirlwind, the result of profound reflections on his art and practice in the face of the delicate balances of the world around him.
B7F74F907B4045FE7BED7BFC266D3A7F: Bury Tomorrow has been a permanent fixture of the metalcore scene for more than twenty years now. Since forming in Southampton in 2006, the band has become one of the most prominent names on the British heavy scene , with eight albums under their belt. In 2025, they released the album Will You Haunt Me, With That Same Patience . It is raw, emotional and intense. A mix of dread, self-destruction and the search for peace in a chaotic world. The band worked with producer Carl Bown ( Sleep Token , Bullet For My Valentine , While She Sleeps ) for the first time, resulting in their most personal, ambitious and cathartic work to date. As if that weren’t enough, the line-up is complemented by Stick To Your Guns , Elwood Stray AND Windwaker . This promises to be a great night!
C27C24D27B0D8D1F570F5DD5A6184F99: Basement is a British band from Suffolk that effortlessly combines post-hardcore, emo, grunge and alternative rock. Since their debut in 2009, they have become a cult favourite thanks to their mix of gritty guitars, compelling melodies, big choruses and emotional intensity. Albums like Colourmeinkindness , Promise Everything and Beside Myself made them an established name on the international alternative guitar scene. After an eight-year writing hiatus, the five original band members are back with WIRED , their first album since 2018. The album sounds familiar yet ambitious, with influences of R.E.M. , Interpol , The Smashing Pumpkins and a raw production by John Congleton (St. Vincent) . Meanwhile, their 2012 track Covet has been given an unexpected second lease of life thanks to TikTok, resulting in an entire new generation of fans.

The German indie pop band Giant Rooks have been together for over ten years and, with albums such as ROOKERY and How Have You Been?, have become one of Europe’s most successful indie bands. On their third album, If Heaven Exists, This Might Be It, they explore the search for connection in a world full of alienation and uncertainty. On this album, the band expands on their familiar indie pop sound with heavy guitars, dreamy synths and surprising experiments, such as ‘The Waves’ featuring the French singer Solann.

The German music press is enthusiastic; Frontstage Magazine calls it a “compelling, profound and thoroughly successful album”. Giant Rooks are coming to present their new album live. ﻿
D03F0564F4D09001F9F8AB149AE7FE1E: Ferdi is a rising star in the Brussels-Paris music scene in recent years. He lives in the Belgian capital and is originally from France. After 15 years of training at the conservatory, he decided to pursue a career in music production, quickly becoming a key figure on the current scene and launching his solo project. He soon began collaborating with artists such as pianist Sofiane Pamart, the king of funk Dabeull, and his friend, trumpeter Béesau. Following his critically acclaimed debut solo EP, “Val Duchesse,” he decided to collaborate with Dabeull on an album that bridges their two musical worlds. This musical collaboration quickly became a natural fit, and the result can be enjoyed on the album “ Romance ,” released on September 8, 2024. In the vein of his first EP, Ferdi released his debut solo album, “TAKE 01,” in 2024, blending jazz and indie-pop.

What a year Madison McFerrin has had! In April 2025, she gave an impressive Tiny Desk concert, followed by the release of her second album, SCORPIO, in June—an album that made an even bigger impression than her debut. She capped off the series with a guest appearance on Tyler, The Creator’s song “Don’t You Worry Baby,” from his surprise album Don’t Top The Glass, released in July. Her second album has a cinematic quality and provides a vibrant backdrop for McFerrin’s voice, which sounds both powerful and angelic. The album earned her countless covers in leading music magazines, accompanied by rave reviews.

The confident woman we hear on SCORPIO has risen from the ashes of a broken relationship. After years of struggle, Madison ended the relationship with her then-fiancé and manager. “We were supposed to get married today / but instead I’m here, all alone / in a house / with no one who’s mine,” Madison sings in the revealing track “I Don’t”—a song that, according to Billboard , conveys a feeling that lies somewhere between sadness and the euphoria of liberation.

Madison McFerrin sings her way through the various stages of heartbreak, with vocal agility and her signature, captivating harmonies (perhaps inspired by her father, jazz singer Bobby McFerrin) . The album is meticulously arranged with layered vocal parts set against a backdrop of house, soul, and jazz, which never fail to captivate the listener.
DDB43DDFF234FF6DCCA0A58E448C906E: Phoenician Drive takes its name from the ancient people of what is modern-day Lebanon, known for their commercial acumen and cultural influence across the Mediterranean region. The Brussels-based sextet was established by Chilean percussionist Diego Moscoso and combines psychedelic rock-'n-roll with traditional music. The great diversity of musical traditions that are still very much alive today in Turkey, the Middle East, Cyprus, Greece, North Africa, Sicily, Andalusia and countless other regions forms an endless playground for them. The band explores, experiments and strays from the beaten path, to then reshape beats and motifs and give them new form and meaning. Tracks slowly crystallise from an anachronistic, syncretic melting pot, while the six musicians create a space in which the electric oud and darbuka blend freely with distorted guitars and contemporary pop. After two EPs - Two Coins for the Boatman and GLOW – and an eponym album, Phoenician Drive will release a second EP on EXAG Records in early 2027. Shadowboxing will be an album with eight songs and is a call to peaceful resistance in our surreal modern times. Themes like dictatorship, covid lockdowns and the post-Soviet era are encapsulated in short, absurdist choruses and long, trance-like musical arrangements in which beings from the past appear and dance beneath broken street lamps.
DF95B96B34BC9429D87DF15843622C87: Alice Mae – whose real name is Alexia – used to pinch her parent’s CDs to immerse herself in classic alternative rock. Inspired by legendary bands like Oasis , The Rolling Stones and U2 , she promised herself she would make authentic, no-nonsense rock music, with a distinctly female edge in a predominantly male scene. At the age of 25, she delivered on that promise. Her style reflects her easy-going nature, yet at the same time she touches you deeply with her unique, well-worn voice. Alice Mae sings with raw sincerity and has an exceptional way of conveying her feelings straight to the hearts of her audience. She writes music to create order in her chaotic mind and pours her thoughts into lyrics in the hope that they become something meaningful. With her raw voice, passion for music and lively personality, Alice Mae promises to be an artist who not only touches hearts but also lifts spirits. Welcome to her club of ‘Messed Up Grown Ups’!

Seduced by the inner song of the flora, they emerged from the moss. The origin story of the Gothenburg-based music collective Fauna explains it all. In early 2023, the debut singles ‘Animalisk’ and ‘Cirkel’ were released, featuring that unique, driving sound which has since garnered widespread acclaim from both audiences and critics alike. By combining organic instrumentation with danceable beats, the tracks offered a captivating introduction to their artistic identity.

Following these releases, the band’s first live performance took place in March 2023, during an underground club night organised by the collective itself in Gothenburg, alongside international acts such as Acid Arab and Carbon Based Lifeforms. Since this successful debut and their first music releases, the band has played at countless prestigious festivals across Scandinavia and mainland Europe – including our very own BRDCST. Their debut album, Taiga Trans, was released in early 2026 on Glitterbeat and is essential listening for anyone wishing to fully prepare for a marvellous live experience.

Sudanese singer, oud player, and composer Sulaf blends Nubian-rooted rhythms, devotional traditions, and folk influences into a deeply personal, emotionally charged sound. Her debut album ABA , created with French producer Maxime Kosinetz (Imarhan, Tinariwen), draws on Sufi poetry written by her great-grandfather to explore themes of loss, identity, and resilience.

Originally developed during a short residency in Paris, the project took on new meaning when war in Sudan forced Sulaf into exile to France. The album traces that journey through longing, memory, and spiritual resilience, combining oud, voice, and subtle electronics in a sound that feels both ancient and strikingly modern.

At the heart of Sulaf’s work is her powerful, expressive voice — capable of both intimate vulnerability and soaring intensity. Her music honours the legacy of Sudanese artists while opening new sonic pathways that connect audiences across cultures.
